mandatory_rules: Group all logs sharing the exact same non-null Process ID (PID) into a foundational 'Event Core'. This grouping is absolute and these cores must never be split internally.

Logs that lack a PID, such as those from the 'kernel', system daemons during restart ('syslogd'), or init scripts ('rc', 'network'), are to be treated as individual, single-line 'Event Cores' pending further analysis by heuristic rules.
heuristic_rules: [MERGE EVENT CORES Rule for Network Attack/Scan] After initial PID-based grouping, identify all 'Event Cores' containing templates like 'authentication failure' (TemplateID 197), 'check pass; user unknown' (TemplateID 195), 'connection from' (TemplateID 196), or 'Connection from <*> on illegal port' (TemplateID 249). Merge all such cores, regardless of their original PID or process name (e.g., sshd, ftpd, rshd), if they share the exact same Key Source Identifier (IP address or FQDN from the 'rhost' field) and occur within a 10-minute sliding window. This reconstructs a single logical 'Network Attack' or 'Scan' event from a single external actor.

[BOUNDARY Rule by State Change for Successful Login] An 'Event Core' representing a successful login (e.g., 'session opened for user', TemplateID 168) must not be merged with any preceding 'Network Attack/Scan' event, even if they share the same Key Source Identifier. This successful session initiates its own distinct 'User Session' event and acts as a definitive boundary.

[MERGE EVENT CORES Rule for System Boot] Identify a log with EventTemplate 'Linux version <*>' (TemplateID 3) or 'syslogd ...: restart.' (TemplateID 0) as the trigger for a 'System Boot' event. Greedily merge this trigger with all subsequent logs from the 'kernel' process and any 'Event Cores' whose EventTemplate contains 'startup succeeded' (TemplateID 1). The merge window for this event ends after 4 minutes or upon the first user session log ('session opened for user'), whichever comes first.

[STATE TRANSITION BOUNDARY Rule for Sessions] An 'Event Core' created by the mandatory PID rule is defined as a complete 'User Session' event if it contains both a 'session opened for user' log (TemplateID 168) and a corresponding 'session closed for user' log (TemplateID 169) for the same user. All logs between these two state transition markers that share the same PID belong to this single event.

[MERGE EVENT CORES Rule for Service Restart] Identify an 'Event Core' indicating a service shutdown (e.g., 'cupsd shutdown succeeded', TemplateID 198) or exit ('exiting'). If another 'Event Core' from the same process name (e.g., 'cups') indicating a startup (e.g., 'cupsd startup succeeded', TemplateID 1) occurs within a 60-second window, merge both cores into a single logical 'Service Restart' event.

[MERGE EVENT CORES Rule for System Under Memory Pressure] Identify multiple distinct 'Event Cores' with the template 'Out of Memory: Killed process <*> (<*>)' (TemplateID 254). Merge all such cores that occur within a 10-minute window into a single, overarching 'System Under Memory Pressure' event, representing a period of resource exhaustion.

[MERGE EVENT CORES Rule for Kernel Error Trace] Identify a log with an EventTemplate indicating a critical kernel error, such as 'page allocation failure' (TemplateID 255). Greedily merge this trigger with all subsequent, contiguous logs from the 'kernel' process that match the stack trace template '[<*>] <*>+<*>' (e.g., TemplateIDs 256-313). This groups the error trigger and its full stack trace into a single 'Kernel Error Trace' event.

[KEY DIMENSION SPLIT Rule for External Actors] When applying any merging rule based on a Key Source Identifier (e.g., 'rhost'), if the identifier's value changes (e.g., from IP '1.2.3.4' to '5.6.7.8'), a new logical event must be started. 'Event Cores' originating from distinct external actors must never be merged into the same event.
